thread:
sophia: quick heads-up — Customer Alpha pushed back: they want GA-level SLA of 99.95% + 50ms p95 for short-text hosted plan. asking if we can commit and what tradeoffs look like.

alex: whoa — 50ms p95 is pretty tight, especially across multi-tenant hosted. current promise is 99.9% and p95 ~120ms on our small text model.

mike: +1. also need to know request distribution (seq length, concurrency). 50ms might be possible with dedicated pools + ngraph/kernels but not for bursty tenants.

jin: what's their commercial posture? are they expecting enterprise pricing or trying to leverage GA to push us?

sophia: they're in pilot, low commit today, but said they will convert to Dedicated with higher commit if GA supports their SLA. so it's a negotiation lever.

ella: observability note — we don't have route-level p95 per-customer in console. we only have cluster-level and model-level histograms. building per-tenant p95 dashboards + alerting is ~2w dev effort + 1wk infra.

alex: rough engineering estimate to hit 50ms p95: 1) dedicated GPU scheduling per-tenant (reserve capacity) 2) quantized model variant pinned for that tenant 3) KV cache prefilling for expected prefixes. overall ~3-4w cross-team plus soak test.

rachel: finance perspective — if we promise that SLA, we need a surcharge and minimum commit to cover reserved capacity risk. propose +35% margin on top of Dedicated list price or a 6mo minimum.

mike: also need a fallback policy for when we miss p95 SLA. do we offer credits? automatic fallback to lower SLA model?

sophia: customer wants guaranteed failover to regional replica; wants credits for downtime and a technical point of contact.

alex: I'd push for a staged GA promise: 1) GA = 99.9% uptime + documented perf profile; 2) SLA 99.95 + 50ms offered as "Dedicated enterprise" add-on with commitment and surcharge.

jin: agree. this preserves GA while creating a path for the customer's ask.

ella: action item: add per-tenant latency dashboards (owner: ella, ETA: 2026-04-02).

alex: action item: engineering spec for Dedicated-SLA variant (owner: alex, ETA: 2026-04-09). include required autoscale, KV cache, and kernel pinning steps.

rachel: action item: pricing proposal and legal SLA template (owner: rachel, ETA: 2026-04-06). include credit calculation and minimum commit.

mike: action item: create a soak test plan and SLO burn-in criteria (owner: mike, ETA: 2026-04-16). propose 2 weeks of steady-state at target load with <1% breach.

oncall-bot: deploy-notify: created incident runbook draft: "dedicated-sla-fallback" (link: https://phabricator/repo/runbooks/dedicated-sla-fallback).

jin: question — do we need legal sign-off to advertise 99.95 for GA vs Dedicated?

sophia: yes. we'll only market 99.9 GA. any higher SLA must have legal review and dedicated contract.

alex: proposal for the customer reply: "We can meet your availability/performance goal as a Dedicated Enterprise offering with a minimum commitment and surge pricing. For GA, we will ship 99.9% with improved route-level monitoring; per-tenant 99.95 commitments require contract & deployment changes."

sophia: agreed. I'll draft the customer-facing note and share.

ella: note — monitoring deliverable also unlocks telemetry for billing and post-launch regressions. makes sense to prioritize.

rachel: I'll draft the price uplift + credit matrix and circulate for review.

mike: ok. next sync in standup Thursday to confirm spec links and docs.

sophia: thanks all — owners: ella, alex, rachel, mike. keep updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
